history.value: With comparisons one turn deep (decision/one-turn-comparisons) a lane's reads cost minutes (cell gauntlet 2-3, mutate bench 3, boss replay 5, a 399-game burst 1.5, a headline read 12-33 per 500 sequences; measurement/cost@gauntlet, jobs 0184-0191): lane sequential-bursts spent 1.2 cpu-h where the two lanes before it spent 42 on two-turn reads. A lane's queued work is gone within the hour, so lanes wait on code and specs, and the CPU idles meanwhile. Planning rules: a candidate's CPU-hours hardly rank it (its code cost does); code-free probes on existing nets and files are what fills the machine meanwhile; statistical power is cheap, so one-turn reads take the wider n (three burst seeds, both books) by default; the long jobs left are the full test suite, depth questions and the product's reported two-turn score. Exits: training on new content at scale (packs after runtime-registry stage 3), or a depth question opened as a lane.
